PullRequest.Title: newChatWindow: start with a given agent, input and window options

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a new chat window without options, or with auxiliary-window overrides.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: getNewChatEditorInput -> ChatWidgetService.openSession -> editorService.openEditor -> createAuxiliaryEditorPart -> auxiliaryWindowService.open -> chat editor initialization. Window creation and native registration must finish before the command obtains a widget; this ordering is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: mainWindow.open creates the auxiliary browser/native window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One window per successful command invocation; browser popup retries require explicit user action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same AUX_WINDOW_GROUP opening created one auxiliary window with fixed compact/bounds options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before editor and widget creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read inherited always-on-top state when unspecified, then invoke vscode:registerAuxiliaryWindow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration per native window and one inherited-state query when alwaysOnTop is unspecified. An explicit override can skip the latter query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One registration and the inherited always-on-top query already occurred. The new options do not increase either count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited initialization before the widget is returned.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One new session and one auxiliary window per explicit command invocation. Bounds, compact, and split options do not introduce a collection loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one opening, native always-on-top inheritance precedes window creation and native registration is awaited afterward. Separate invocations remain independent; the diff adds no parallel opening or retry loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A new window is intentional, not cacheable reuse. Existing session/mode initialization retains its existing caches. Omitting options takes the previous opening path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the changed action through openSession, group selection, auxiliary editor construction, and browser/native window services.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native window creation duration is not measured; no increased boundary cardinality or new critical-path boundary was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Auxiliary options parameterize existing one-window work rather than adding fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Prefill the new window's query without submitting it.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After openSession resolves, setInput updates the input editor and refreshes parsed input before any optional agent wait. The visible draft is available while agent loading continues.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the auxiliary window before assigning its input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One window, as in the default scenario; query text introduces no additional window, subprocess, network request, or file read in the traced setInput/setValue/refreshParsedInput path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The action opened the same window but did not accept a draft query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Window initialization precedes draft assignment, unchanged from the existing opening operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One supplied query of length L per invocation; one setInput call and its existing editor-content/parser notifications.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The input assignment and parsing execute synchronously once; the optional mode wait is asynchronous. The action does not invoke chat submission.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new query cache or retained history collection is added. Existing input-state synchronization has a 150 ms debounce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setInput calls setValue and refreshParsedInput; the changed action never calls a request-submission method.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large drafts can cost proportionally more editor/parser work, but no redundant scaling mechanism beyond the requested input initialization is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is one required prefill operation, not repeated or eager hidden submission work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select a built-in or already cached custom agent in the new chat window.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After window initialization, waitForChatMode performs an immediate in-memory lookup and returns without listeners/timer on a hit; setChatMode then updates the selected mode. This is requested initialization, not an additional service fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing background custom-agent discovery lists prompt files and reads/parses files without an existing text model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A cold discovery pass handles F discovered agent files, with at most one read per file lacking a text model in that pass. The service-wide CachedPromise coalesces concurrent discovery consumers and reuses successful results, including empty results, until invalidation. The new name lookup itself adds zero reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the widget already constructed ChatModes and scheduled the same discovery. No new discovery invocation is made by waitForChatMode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cached mode hit does not wait for this existing refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One requested mode name. Built-in lookup is bounded; custom-name lookup materializes, filters, sorts, and scans M existing modes. The selection occurs once per invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Immediate Promise resolution followed by one mode update. Existing background ChatModes refresh remains delayed/coalesced by its 100 ms Delayer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ChatModes already loads workspace-cached custom modes during construction. A name hit uses that state immediately. The helper does not create another ChatModes instance or invalidate discovery caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced ChatModes construction, cached-mode loading, findModeByName, the immediate helper return, and setChatMode with storeSelection=false.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mode counts and selection-side UI update duration are not measured; a single user-command lookup does not establish a meaningful repeated-work regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added lookup/selection is bounded requested work and does not multiply discovery boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Wait for a late custom agent, time out for an absent agent, or close the widget while waiting.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Only command completion and requested mode selection await the helper, for at most 5 seconds or until widget removal. The window and optional draft already exist and remain usable. Waiting for the requested late agent is intentional behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Previously scheduled agent discovery may finish and publish available modes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The existing shared discovery computation reads up to F files lacking text models per cold/invalidated pass, subject to the service-wide limiter. Warm discovery reuses its promise. Waiting for one name adds no discovery pass and no per-name file read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery ran during widget initialization, but this command did not offer late-agent selection or await its result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery completion can now determine when the requested mode is selected and the command resolves, but is not awaited before displaying the window or query. Timeout bounds this requested wait.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For a provider-backed session type, delegate agent/customization enumeration to the harness item provider, which may be extension-backed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same provider enumeration per existing coalesced ChatModes refresh; the new helper only listens to results and adds zero provider calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider-backed ChatModes initialization already performed this enumeration. The diff does not invoke the provider from the wait loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider completion can affect requested late-agent selection, bounded by the helper timeout; ordinary window opening has already completed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One pending waiter per explicit new-window invocation; O(E) lookups over M modes for mode-collection replacements/change events during the bounded wait. There is no polling or per-file listener in the helper.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each waiter owns one autorun, one replaceable modes listener, one widget-removal listener, and one timeout. settle disposes the store on success/removal/timeout. Discovery reads are queued on the existing service-wide limiter; the helper introduces no new read concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The helper observes existing mode state without refreshing it. A missing name subscribes rather than repeatedly fetching; no persistent negative-name cache or growing retained-name map is added. Underlying discovery retains its existing shared positive/empty cache and invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded waiting, event cardinality, cleanup ownership, and unchanged discovery calls. Provider-internal implementation is outside the available call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual agent-load times, event counts, and external provider behavior are unmeasured. No in-repository caller passes the new options, so downstream extension sequencing cannot be established from this snapshot.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new bounded wait implements requested semantics without polling, retained resources beyond completion, or extra boundary calls; no independently avoidable latency mechanism is proven.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the sole changed file and all four hunks against base 7180cded2f1e73361a4545f5c0fdc2a46532e55a. Traced window creation/native IPC, query initialization, cached and cold agent discovery, shared concurrency/caches, and waiter cleanup. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix was identified. Review is static; external provider internals and option-using extension workflows are unavailable.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
